family_built: exact rational dual certificate for the Delsarte two-point LP bound on spherical codes (Appendix A; k=2 case of the k-point bounds of Section 1; the k=3 analogue is Section 3, eq. (3.1))
verdict: REJECTED on H, on both Track A and Track B

G_generatable.note: the certificate is planted first: f(t) = (t+1)(t-s) prod_i (t-a_i)^2 is non-positive on [-1,s] by inspection; no LP or search runs in make_instance

operations: sign comparison of f_k over Q
Yun squarefree decomposition + Sturm root count (gvlib.roots) for the odd-multiplicity part
V_verifiable.number_of_valid_certificates: infinite -- the accepted set is a full-dimensional convex cone section; enumerate_all() returns None honestly

domain_standard_attack.name: exact rational max-margin (Chebyshev-centre) LP over Q, two-phase simplex with Bland's rule, cutting planes on the continuum constraint
domain_standard_attack.why_this_one: the family asks for FEASIBILITY, so the standard method is to maximise the slack, not to minimise the objective

domain_standard_attack_minimising_varian.name: same simplex, but minimising f(1) instead of maximising the slack
domain_standard_attack_minimising_varian.note: fails only because a minimiser lands exactly on the boundary of the discretised cone and is generically infeasible between grid points; this is an artefact of the objective, not hardness

in_context_tool_free_attack.name: one-parameter repeated-root sweep: f = (t+1)(t-s)(t-a)^{2m}, a swept over 11 rationals
in_context_tool_free_attack.note: Track B requires a fourth in-context attack that FAILS.  This one succeeds 80-90% of the time inside a compact-route budget.

scaling_closure.statement: if f is accepted with f(1) = V, then for lambda = (B-1)/(V-1) >= 1 the certificate lambda*f + (1-lambda) is also accepted and has f(1) = B exactly
scaling_closure.cost: one rational division plus d multiplications
scaling_closure.consequence: tightening the published condition to f(1) == B does not rescue the family

root_cause: the quantity the certificate bounds is the OPTIMUM of the LP, which is a function of (n, d, s) alone.  A generator can plant a feasible dual certificate but not an optimal one, so the published bound is always strictly slack and the accepted set is full-dimensional.
